On appreciation of evidence as adduced by the parties in support of their respective versions, the issue-wise findings of this Tribunal are reproduced herein below:
Whether on 03.01.2019 at about 6.30 pm, on Outer ring Road, near Haiderpur Metro Station, Delhi, one Activa Scooty bearing registration No. DL6A-SP-5837, which was being driven rashly and negligently by Ashish Kumar, hit motorcycle bearing registration No. DL11-SX-1384 and caused injuries to Anita?
OPP 16.
The onus of proving this issue on preponderance of probabilities was upon the petitioner/claimant.
For deciding the present issue, the testimony of PW1 Smt. Anita Devi is relevant, being an eyewitness as well as the injured.

PW1 deposed that on 03.01.2019, at about 6.30 pm, when she was returning from Model Town, Delhi, to her house, with her son Amit, on his motorcycle, bearing registration no. DL-11SX-1384, and they reached at Ring Road, Haiderpur Metro Station, Delhi, they were hit by one Scooty, bearing registration no. DL-6ASP-5837.

She further deposed that the offending vehicle was driven in a rash and negligent manner, by its driver/R1 Ashish and as a result of the said impact, she alongwith her son Amit fell down on the road and sustained injuries.

She further deposed that after the accident, she was taken to Santom Hospital, Prashant Vihar, Delhi, by one scooty rider, whereas her son has brought the driver/R1 Ashish, along with him, to the said MACT No. 170/19 Page 12 of33 Anita vs Ashish Kumar and Ors.
Page 13 of33 hospital.
She further deposed that as per her MLC No. 629/19, she has sustained grievous injuries in the case accident.

17. PW1 was also cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for the insurance company/R3, which was adopted by Ld. Counsel for R2, but, both R3 and R2 failed to impeach the credibility of PW1 and failed to Anita Devi vs Ashish Kumar on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28952906/
7 elicit any admission, from the testimony of PW1, so as to prove that the alleged accident had not taken place with the offending vehicle or due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.

Though, during the course of cross examination of PW1, a suggestion was put to PW1, that the accident took place, because of negligence on the part of drivers of both the vehicles, as they were trying to overtake each other but, PW1 denied the said suggestion.

Thus, the testimony of PW1 on the said aspect went unrebutted and same prima facie proves that the accident, in which PW1 has sustained injuries, has taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.
18.

It is worthwhile to mention here that the though the driver of the offending vehicle/R1 filed his written statement, in which he has taken the defence that at the time of accident, the son of PW1 was negligent, as he was driving his motorcycle, in a rash, negligent and zigzag manner and has applied sudden brakes, due to which, the offending vehicle MACT No. 170/19 Page 13 of33 Anita vs Ashish Kumar and Ors.
Page 14 of33 got struck with the motorcycle, however, R1 failed to prove his defence, either by cross-examination of PW1 or by leading any positive evidence, in his defence.
Thus, he fails to prove absence of negligence, on his part, resulting in the case accident.
19. Further, there is nothing on record which will prove that R1 was falsely implicated in this case by the IO, in connivance with the petitioner.
Further, R1 also failed to prove that he has ever approached to any higher authority, with respect to his false implication in the present case.
Consequently, in view of the unrebutted testimony of PW1, it stands duly proved that the accident had taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.

24. In this context, a perusal of the MLC No. 629/19, of the petitioner Anita, reveals that after examination of the petitioner, the doctor has given the opinion that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the case accident, as she has suffered fracture of clavicle.
It was also observed in the MLC, that the petitioner has sustained injuries over head, left shoulder and right knee.
Perusal of the record further reveals that the petitioner remains admitted at Santom hospital from 03.01.2019 to 06.01.2019.

Therefore, keeping in view the grievous nature of injuries as sustained by the petitioner, the treatment cum recuperation period, in case of the petitioner is determined to be about 06 months and during this period, the petitioner must have incurred expenses on special diet,
